ME-32: a single bounded neurogenic-bladder association has been authored from spinal-cord-infarction clinical literature; the draft-safe association stands until qualified-human review.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-32 adds this relationship only as a bounded neurogenic-bladder association. Anterior cord syndrome from spinal cord infarction produces corticospinal and spinothalamic tract injury below the lesion, and spinal-cord-infarction clinical literature documents neurogenic bladder with urinary incontinence among the disabling complications of the resulting paraplegia, but the primary diagnosis alone does not establish persistent incontinence in every person or determine an individual's recovery course. Require independently documented anterior cord syndrome by imaging and clinical examination, documented urinary incontinence by urodynamic or validated assessment compatible in chronology, and specialist review. Preserve pre-existing urologic disease, diabetes, prostate pathology in men, medication effects, and other competing causes of incontinence.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of anterior cord syndrome by MRI and neurologic examination
Documented urinary incontinence by urodynamic study or validated assessment with chronology
Assessment of pre-existing urologic disease, diabetes, prostate pathology, and medications
Specialist assessment distinguishing cord-injury-related incontinence from other causes

sourceReferences.citation: Thomas G, Alakbarzade V, Sammaraiee Y, et al. Spontaneous spinal cord infarction: a practical approach. Pract Neurol. 2022;22(6):497-502. PMID 35835550. doi:10.1136/pn-2022-003441.
sourceReferences.note: Practical clinical review of spinal cord infarction documenting neurogenic bladder and bowel dysfunction among the complications arising from the resulting paraplegia. It supports a bounded disease-association proposition and clinical evaluation, not automatic individual causation or aggravation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 35835550; neurogenic bladder and bowel complications of spinal cord infarction

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Spinal cord infarction causing anterior cord syndrome is documented to produce neurogenic bladder with urinary incontinence among its complications, but the clinical literature does not establish an individual medical nexus without documentation of both the cord lesion and the incontinence, compatible chronology, and competing-cause review.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by this association evidence; the mapping is not an individual nexus opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Infarction of the anterior spinal artery territory disrupts descending suprasacral control of the detrusor and sphincter, producing neurogenic detrusor overactivity or overflow with urge and overflow incontinence, but the individual pathway must be established from urodynamic studies and neurologic evaluation.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Neurogenic bladder is a documented complication of spinal cord infarction, but the literature does not establish that anterior cord syndrome caused or aggravated urinary incontinence in every individual, and partial recovery is common; both diagnoses, chronology, urodynamic findings, and competing etiologies require case-specific review.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented cord syndrome and incontinence; chronology and recovery course; urodynamic findings; urologic, diabetic, prostatic, and medication alternatives; specialist assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pre-existing urologic disease, benign prostatic obstruction, or pelvic-floor weakness
Medication effects including diuretics and sedatives
